convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load an external custom indicator 'iVLT' for signal generation. The signal logic depends on a custom indicator buffer that cannot be replicated with built-in MT5 indicators alone. Pending order management with global variables adds complexity.

derived_values.name: BuyStopPrice: previous bar High + (PendingLevel + Spread) points
SellStopPrice: previous bar Low - PendingLevel points

other_exits: When a position is opened (detected via Pos.Select), all remaining pending stop orders are deleted (DeleteStops function). This prevents multiple fills from stale pending orders.

custom_logic_notes: The EA places BOTH BuyStop and SellStop simultaneously on every new signal (no existing position + no pending stops). It uses global variables (gvp+'bs', gvp+'ss') as a deferred execution mechanism: signal sets GV on new bar, then on subsequent ticks the pending orders are placed when price data is available. If a position is detected later, all opposing/remaining stop orders are deleted via CheckDelete flag. The iVLT indicator buffer 2 (index 2) is checked at bar [1] — if it is not EMPTY_VALUE, a signal fires. The SL/TP are calculated relative to the pending order price, not the current market price, and are clamped to respect broker StopsLevel minimums. SellStop does NOT add spread to the offset distance (unlike BuyStop which adds spread), creating an asymmetry.
python_conversion_notes: Requires reverse-engineering or obtaining the iVLT custom indicator source to replicate buffer 2 calculation. The global variable deferred-execution pattern (signal on bar N, place pending orders on subsequent ticks) can be simplified to direct pending order placement on bar close in Python. Pay attention to the asymmetric spread handling: BuyStop price = prev High + (PendingLevel+Spread)*Point, SellStop price = prev Low - PendingLevel*Point. The StopsLevel clamping logic for SL/TP must be preserved. The dual pending order placement (both BuyStop and SellStop simultaneously) means the first to fill determines direction; the other is deleted once a position exists.
